title: Best 60-Pint Dehumidifier (2026): Pump, Hose & Real Ratings
h1: The Best 60-Pint Dehumidifiers for Big, Wet Basements
dek: Sixty pints is a lot of water to pull from the air — so make sure the number on the box means what you think it does.
description: The best 60-pint dehumidifier for 2026: Midea, Frigidaire and Costway picks, what the 2019 DOE re-rating means for the label, and pump vs. hose drainage.
intro: A **60-pint dehumidifier** is for the spaces a 50-pint can't quite tame: a large basement that smells musty all summer, a lower level with sweating pipes, or an open floor plan in a humid climate. Our top pick is the **Midea 60-Pint Dehumidifier with Pump**, because it pairs that capacity with a built-in pump, so the biggest chore at this size, hauling a full bucket, simply disappears.

Three things matter most at this size: where the 60 comes from (older and marketing ratings often run higher than today's DOE figures), how the water will drain, and what it costs to run for months on end. Below are three 60-pint picks plus two true 50-pint alternatives that can match an old-scale "60".
topPicksLead: The **Midea 60-Pint Dehumidifier with Pump** is the best 60-pint dehumidifier for most wet basements, combining big listed capacity with a pump and an included drain hose.

Federal efficiency minimum for portable units above 50 pints a day

blocks.text: Colder test air yields less water, so every rating dropped when the DOE switched procedures. A **true** DOE 60 is a big machine; a "60" from an older or saturated-air test may be a mid-40s unit by today's yardstick.

We don't run a test lab. We compare each model's listed and DOE capacity, ENERGY STAR data, manuals and coverage claims, check CPSC recall records, and read owner reviews for patterns such as pump failures, defrost problems and units that shut off early. Every pick here is a verified Amazon listing.
Because 60-pint labels are inconsistent, we also included two genuine DOE 50-pint units, and we flag where a listing doesn't say which test its number came from.

items.label: Find out which test the 60 comes from
items.text: Look for "DOE" or the ENERGY STAR listing. A 60 measured in hot, saturated air, or on the pre-2019 test, isn't comparable to a current DOE 60.

items.label: Size for wetness, not just square feet
items.text: Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) puts wet spaces over 2,000 square feet at 50+ DOE pints. A 60 makes sense for seepage, sweating walls or a big open lower level; a musty 1,200-square-foot basement doesn't need one.

items.label: Decide on drainage first
items.text: At this size a bucket is a backup, not a plan.
sub: Floor drain or sump below the outlet: a gravity hose
Drain is higher, or across the room: a built-in pump
No drain at all: pump to a laundry sink or out a window

items.label: Auto-defrost for cool basements
items.text: Below about 65°F, coils can frost. Auto-defrost keeps the unit working through spring and fall instead of icing up.

items.label: Running cost
items.text: A basement unit may run thousands of hours a year. ENERGY STAR certification, or a published L/kWh figure, tells you what each pint costs. See our [electricity guide](/guides/how-much-electricity-does-a-dehumidifier-use/) for the math.

items.label: Controls you can see
items.text: A digital humidistat with an exact percentage and a clear humidity readout lets you hold 45–50% instead of running flat out.

sections.heading: What "60 pints" means after the 2019 DOE re-rating

blocks.text: Before 2019, dehumidifiers were rated in 80°F air at 60% humidity. The DOE now tests at 65°F, closer to a real basement, and ratings fell by roughly 30%: yesterday's 70-pinter is today's 50-pinter. Our [70-pint guide](/best/best-70-pint-dehumidifier/) shows how brands handled the switch.

blocks.text: Why true 60-pint DOE ratings are rare

Most mainstream portable lines top out at 50 DOE pints; going bigger means a larger compressor and the strictest federal efficiency class. A few genuine DOE 60s do exist, such as Danby's 60-pint with pump and Wi-Fi, covered in our [Danby guide](/best/best-danby-dehumidifier/), and the Pelonis 60-pint with pump. Beyond that, the next real step up is a crawl-space or commercial unit; see our [100-pint guide](/best/best-100-pint-dehumidifier/).

sections.heading: Pump vs. hose: draining a 60-pint dehumidifier

blocks.text: Sixty pints is 7.5 gallons a day at full output, so even a generous 1.7-gallon tank would fill in under six hours, then the unit shuts off until you empty it. Real output drops as the room nears your setpoint, but a wet basement in July still means more than one trip a day.

items: **Gravity hose:** a garden hose runs downhill from the drain port to a floor drain or sump. Nothing to fail; raise the unit on a sturdy platform if needed.
**Built-in pump:** pushes water up to a laundry sink or out a window when your only drain sits higher than the outlet.
**Bucket only:** fine for a few days, not a plan at this size.

blocks.title: Pump tip
blocks.text: Clip the end of the pump line so it can't slip out of the sink, and check it each spring for algae or kinks. A blocked line is the most common reason owners find a pump model stopped.

items: **Your basement is big and wet, with no drain below the unit:** the Midea 60-Pint with Pump.
**There's a floor drain or sump nearby and you want a familiar brand:** the Frigidaire 60-Pint on a gravity hose.
**You want the 60-pint label for less and have a drain:** the Costway 60-Pint, which adds auto-defrost for chilly floors.
**Your basement is damp rather than flooded and running cost matters:** the Midea Cube 50, ENERGY STAR certified with a big reservoir.

blocks.text: A 60-pint dehumidifier earns its size in big, genuinely wet basements, and the Midea 60-Pint with Pump is the easiest to live with because it drains itself. The Frigidaire and Costway 60s suit spaces with a floor drain. If you can't confirm a 60's DOE rating, a true 50-pinter is a safe, often equally capable bet. For more placement ideas, see our [basement dehumidifier guide](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-basement/).

faqs.a: For most large, wet basements, the Midea 60-Pint Dehumidifier with Pump, because it drains itself to a sink or window. If you have a floor drain, the Frigidaire 60-Pint on a gravity hose is a simpler choice, and the Costway 60-Pint is the value pick.

faqs.q: Is the Frigidaire 60-pint dehumidifier worth it?
faqs.a: It's a good fit for a big basement with a floor drain, backed by a widely serviced brand. Frigidaire has sold 60-pint units under model numbers such as FFAD6022W1 (marketed as a High Humidity 60-pint) and FFAD6023W1, so check the model number and rating label of the unit you're buying.

faqs.q: What size area does a 60-pint dehumidifier cover?
faqs.a: Our picks' listings claim 4,000 to 5,500 square feet, but those are best cases. In practice, a 60-pint suits a wet basement or open lower level of roughly 2,000 square feet or more; dampness matters more than floor area.

faqs.q: Is a 60-pint dehumidifier better than a 50-pint?
faqs.a: Only if both are rated on the same test. A DOE 2019 60-pinter removes more water than a DOE 50, but a 60 from the old or saturated-air test can be smaller than a modern 50. Compare DOE figures, not box labels.

faqs.q: Are the Pelonis and Danby 60-pint dehumidifiers with pump any good?
faqs.a: Both are genuine 60-pint pump models. The Danby adds Wi-Fi and a two-year parts-and-labor warranty; the Pelonis is efficient for its class but not ENERGY STAR certified.

faqs.q: Should I buy an older 60-pint model like the Comfort-Aire BHDP-60A?
faqs.a: Be cautious with older or secondhand 60-pint units. Older models were often rated on the pre-2019 test, and several brands, Comfort-Aire among them, have been part of large dehumidifier recalls. Look up any model number on the CPSC recall site before you plug it in.
